newsitem.title: USA: US Prods Outlook - Buyers seen returning in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: US Prods Outlook - Buyers seen returning in Chicago.

text.p: As trade in U.S. spot products markets opened on Monday, buyers were expected to re-emerge in Chicago, where a court order cleared the way for a key regional refiner to resume full production, traders said.
And in New York Harbor, cold weather that swept through the Northeast over the weekend could fuel increased heating oil demand and boost differentials back above the print this week, traders said.

Nationwide, distillate stocks last week were reported 13.9 million barrels below the same week last year and gasoline stocks were 6.2 million barrels lower, but a 9.3 million barrel crude build signaled the end of autumn turnarounds.
"We're coming out of the turnarounds and out of the problems, but there's still a slight chance of some firecrackers," a Gulf Coast trader said of the outlook in the always volatile cash markets.

In the Midwest, spot gasoline buyers had raced to the sidelines last Friday after an Illinois court allowed Clark Refining and Marketing Co to restart two units at its Chicago-area refinery idled after a fire in October.

The decision shaved a premium off of unleaded gasoline in Chicago that had been building since Clark shut two processing units and trimmed runs at its Blue Island, Illinois refinery after the October 19 fire.
"I'm short, but I can live with it right now," said one trader willing to wait out the sellers as diffs eased two cents a gallon on Friday, offsetting higher futures prices.
Clark's 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island refinery had trimmed production levels to 55,000 barrels per day in the wake of the explosion and fire that idled an alkylation unit and propane scrubber.
But after the court decision was released, Clark said it would double gasoline output to two million gallons per day or over 47,500 barrels per day "as soon as possible."
"This is going to push differentials down, especially for any (month) deliveries," another Chicago trader said.
Relatively high prices in the Midwest were expected to draw additional barrels from the Gulf coast, traders said.

The Williams pipeline system, a barometer of stocks in the Group Three market centered in Kansas City, Missouri reported a 19-day supply of gasoline, 32-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 46-day supply of high-sulphur diesel on hand.
The scheduled weekend return of Amuay's big cat cracker in Venezuela -- combined with the stepped-up production by Clark in the Midwest -- looks likely to take pressure off U.S. gasoline prices.
"The Amuay and Clark news have kind of taken the edge off the gasoline market," said one trader.
But traders noted maintenance on gasoline-producing units run by Sun Co near Philadelphia and Amerada Hess on St Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands is keeping tightness in focus.

Also, Colonial Pipeline's move to open up a gasoline line to speed shipments of heating oil to the huge Northeast home heating oil market has tightened gasoline supplies, while flooding New York Harbor with more distillates than the so-far mild weather can sustain.

On the West Coast, traders said refined products prices were expected to soften next week, despite a slight rise in CARB-grade gasoline Friday, as steep cuts in retail prices and growing supply put pressure on wholesale prices.
"There's too much gas and that's evidenced by people rolling out of November into December," cargoes, one West Coast broker said
The average retail price of regular unleaded gasoline out west fell 2.4 cents to 136.6 cents a gallon for the week ended November 4.
"I still think it'll be weak unless the street (price) moves up," the broker said.
-- Houston Bureau 713 210-8508
